prompt: Stage 2-1 augment round. You opened with a pair of the 1-cost carry of a reroll line you like. Scouting shows three players holding that carry and one of them already has a pair too. What is your plan?

lobby.note: Pair of your carry on board, AD items
One copy of your carry, holding an AD component
One copy, playing the same trait

options.label: Commit: you have the pair, roll early to win the race
Keep the pair, play a flexible opener, decide at 3-2 based on who drops it
Sell the pair now and buy the tank pair from the shop

explanation:
Three players on a reroll carry means the pool is split four ways; the 3-star needs 9 copies out of a pool that is already 4+ copies lighter. Winning that race from a pair requires rolling gold you do not have at 2-1. But selling now is also wrong: contest at 2-1 is soft. Two of those three players will be pushed off the line by their 2-1 augment or a bad 2-5, and the one who stays is the one you need to know about.

The correct plan is to keep the pair (it costs one bench slot and 2 gold of tempo), play the strongest board for stage 2 regardless of trait, and re-scout at 3-2. If two players are still holding at 3-2, you pivot with no loss; if they dropped it, you were the one who held.
principle: Contest is read at 3-2, not decided at 2-1.
commonMistake: Forcing because "I have the pair". A pair is 2 of 9 copies; it is not a lead.
